content_of_post_to_comment:
Hey everyone,

Right now, my life is in a huge mess. I am trying to fix a long-term issue that I know will take a very long time to resolve, and a lot of it relies on just waiting it out.

I am really struggling with a few things right now:

Every time I start feeling happy or trying to do things that make me happy, I feel like I immediately take 10 steps back. It makes me feel like enjoying myself serves no purpose, and it leaves me distracted and confused.

I have a very limited amount of time to get things done, and the stress is making me feel incredibly depressed. It is getting to the point where I just want to give up and let go.

I am feeling stuck and desperate. How can I make full use of my limited time when the stress is this heavy? How do you maintain discipline and keep moving forward when every positive step feels like it gets wiped out?

Any advice, routines, or perspective shifts would be greatly appreciated. Thank you.
comment: When you feel like every good moment gets punished by a setback, it can make happiness feel unsafe. Something that helped me was separating “feeling better” from “being done fixing things.” You’re allowed to have small moments that recharge you even while the bigger problem is still unresolved. Maybe the goal right now isn’t perfect discipline, but protecting enough energy to keep showing up.
